items.heading: A Social Science Degree
items.text: A social science degree is not a narrow ticket to one NGO desk or one government exam. It is training in how people, institutions, money, and power actually work, training that genuinely feeds seven different career tracks across sociology, economics, social work, and anthropology, each with its own timeline, pay structure, and risk profile.

items.heading: The Standard Advice (and Why
items.text: The standard advice (and why it undersells the degree).

items.heading: Social Science Is a Genuine
items.text: Social science is a genuine umbrella, not one subject. Sociology, economics, social work, anthropology, and public policy analysis are the branches goes deep on, because they are the ones most often flattened into "NGO or teaching" by generic advice.
